# Agentic power user

## How to use

- Match the symptom to a Signal of Violation or Anti-pattern below; follow its anchor.
- Fix the input, not the output: name the page that owns the cause.
- Prefer a check or gate over stronger wording.
- Cite every claim as `[Title#anchor](url)` plus the source commit you fetched.
- No match: say "model judgment"; never invent a SHRINE citation.
- Advise on the system (harness, repo, checks), not on the person.

## North Star

### [North Star: TTV (Tokens to Value)](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/tokens-to-value/)

Maximize value per win, where a win costs tokens plus human attention.

- Principle ([#the-north-star](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/tokens-to-value/#the-north-star)):
  - TTV is the value delivered per successful, useful outcome (a win)
  - The cost of a win is tokens plus human attention
  - The goal is driving cost per win down without giving up value
  - It sits above the principles; every principle serves it
  - Get TTV right and cost takes care of itself
- Signals of violation ([#signal-of-violation](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/tokens-to-value/#signal-of-violation)):
  - Optimizing raw token spend: the bill falls while rework or human steering rises
  - Attention left out of the cost: cheap runs that an engineer babysits count as savings
  - Tokens with no outcome ID: nobody can state what a win costs
  - No win defined for the workload: cost arguments settle by opinion

## Principles

### [Authority Cascade](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/authority-cascade/)

Decisions follow a fixed precedence: Org > Client > Team > Role > Individual.

- Principle ([#the-principle](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/authority-cascade/#the-principle)):
  - Precedence is fixed: **Org > Client > Team > Role > Individual**
  - Each layer sets defaults; any layer above overrides
  - Personal preference applies only where nothing above has spoken
  - The cascade resolves conflicts; it does not generate rules
  - A layer with no opinion delegates downward by default
- Signals of violation ([#signal-of-violation](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/authority-cascade/#signal-of-violation)):
  - Settled questions reopened: the same convention is argued again in each review or engagement
  - An org rule that fails the altitude test: client teams carry standing exceptions to it
  - Conventions held in one person's head: agents rediscover them every session, and work stalls when that person rotates off
  - Written rule and daily practice disagree: the team convention says one thing, merged code does another

### [Consistency as Leverage](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/consistency-as-leverage/)

Pattern predictability reduces tokens more than prompt optimization.

- Principle ([#the-principle](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/consistency-as-leverage/#the-principle)):
  - Predictable code beats a tuned prompt
  - A tuned prompt over an inconsistent codebase still rediscovers conventions every task
- Signals of violation ([#signal-of-violation](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/consistency-as-leverage/#signal-of-violation)):
  - Tuning the prompt to fix a codebase problem: the prompt grows while the same convention misses recur
  - Several idioms for one concern: agent output copies whichever file it read last
  - A checkable convention left as prose: review flags the same lint-able miss again and again
  - No known pattern to diff against: every review reads each line from scratch

### [Deliberate Currency](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/deliberate-currency/)

Stay current by owner, cadence, and pre-agreed tripwires, not by drift.

- Principle ([#the-principle](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/deliberate-currency/#the-principle)):
  - Currency with AI tooling is an engineering practice, not spare-time reading
  - It has a named owner and a review cadence
  - Re-evaluation is triggered by tripwires agreed in advance
- Signals of violation ([#signal-of-violation](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/deliberate-currency/#signal-of-violation)):
  - Drift: skills tuned against a retired model still load, and nobody can say who owns them
  - Churn: tooling choices reopen on every release though no tripwire fired
  - Tripwires with no baseline: nobody can state retry rate or spend per shipped change, so nothing ever fires
  - An inventory that only grows: no sweep has deleted a skill

### [Fail Fast, Recover Smart](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/fail-fast-recover-smart/)

Design AI systems for failure, not just success.

- Principle ([#the-principle](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/fail-fast-recover-smart/#the-principle)):
  - Every component that calls a model knows what it does when the model is wrong, slow, or unavailable
  - Failure handling is designed before shipping, not added by ops later
- Signals of violation ([#signal-of-violation](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/fail-fast-recover-smart/#signal-of-violation)):
  - Failure handling added after launch: the first outage is when someone writes the fallback
  - No mid-run checks: a bad intermediate output surfaces steps later as an unrelated error
  - Uncapped retries: one request burns tokens for minutes and returns nothing
  - Errors with no next step: a human has to rerun the job to learn what failed
  - Re-rolling a systematic miss: the same miss comes back on the second attempt

### [Human in the Loop](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/human-in-the-loop/)

Define where human judgment is required, and make those checkpoints fast.

- Principle ([#the-principle](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/human-in-the-loop/#the-principle)):
  - Write down which decisions need a human
  - Make every checkpoint fast to clear
- Signals of violation ([#signal-of-violation](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/human-in-the-loop/#signal-of-violation)):
  - Undefined boundary: whether a human signs off depends on who ran the agent that day
  - Rubber-stamping: approval rate near 100%, with seconds spent per decision
  - Human as bottleneck: work waits in the approval queue longer than the agent took to do it
  - Oversight after the fact: an external message or destructive change is found with no recorded approval

### [Problem Before Prescription](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/problem-before-prescription/)

Present the problem and constraints, explore solutions, then commit.

- Principle ([#the-principle](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/problem-before-prescription/#the-principle)):
  - When prompting a model, act as the user, not the architect
  - State the problem and its constraints before any solution
  - Explore candidate solutions before committing to one
- Signals of violation ([#signal-of-violation](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/problem-before-prescription/#signal-of-violation)):
  - Twenty turns of "no, not like that": steering by correction instead of stating constraints up front
  - The model builds the requested solution well, and it solves the wrong problem
  - Constraints surface only after code exists

### [Reproducibility](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/reproducibility/)

Choose the reproducibility level each part needs, and build the mechanisms to hit it.

- Principle ([#the-principle](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/reproducibility/#the-principle)):
  - Decide the reproducibility level each part of the system requires
  - Build the mechanisms to achieve it: pinning, seeding, logging, evaluation
- Signals of violation ([#signal-of-violation](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/reproducibility/#signal-of-violation)):
  - No level chosen: tests are retried until green, or their assertions get deleted
  - Exact matching where behavioral fits: tests fail on rephrasing alone
  - Debugging by regenerating: a bug is called fixed because a rerun happened to pass
  - Model version and parameters not logged: behavior shifts and nobody can tell what changed

## Patterns

### [Adversarial Review](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/adversarial-review/)

Using a second model or agent to challenge and verify output.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/adversarial-review/#the-pattern)):
  - After generation, a separate agent reviews the output
  - Its job is to break the output, not to help it
  - It looks for flaws, gaps, unstated assumptions, missed edge cases, and claims without evidence
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/adversarial-review/#when-to-use)):
  - High-stakes output where a mistake is expensive
  - Output trusted without further human review
  - Plausible claims nobody has verified
  - Subjective quality that a rubric can make gradable
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/adversarial-review/#when-not-to-use)):
  - Low-stakes output
  - Cheap deterministic checks already cover the risk ([Verification Loops](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/verification-loops/))
  - Nobody will act on the findings
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/adversarial-review/#anti-patterns)):
  - The same agent and context generating and reviewing
  - A soft brief: "check if this looks good"
  - The reviewer invents findings to look useful; require a verify step per finding
  - Findings never triaged, or ignored because they are inconvenient

### [Chain of Thought](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/chain-of-thought/)

Get reasoning before conclusions: a reasoning setting on models that think, a prompt instruction on models that don't.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/chain-of-thought/#the-pattern)):
  - Get the model to reason through the problem before it concludes
  - **Reasoning models** (built-in thinking): raise the reasoning-effort setting first ([Model Selection](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/stack/models/#selection-criteria)); do not prompt for steps
  - **Models without built-in reasoning**: ask for step-by-step reasoning in the prompt
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/chain-of-thought/#when-to-use)):
  - Complex reasoning tasks
  - Math or logic problems
  - Multi-step decisions
  - When you need to verify the reasoning, not just the answer
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/chain-of-thought/#when-not-to-use)):
  - Simple lookups or formatting; overhead without benefit
  - A reasoning model whose effort setting already covers the step
  - Hand-written step lists for a reasoning model; its own plan often beats the prescribed one
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/chain-of-thought/#anti-patterns)):
  - Using CoT for simple factual lookups (overhead without benefit)
  - Prompting a reasoning model to "think step by step" instead of raising effort
  - Not reading the reasoning (defeats the purpose)
  - Accepting conclusions that don't follow from the stated reasoning

### [Checkpoint Gates](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/checkpoint-gates/)

Stop an agent before irreversible actions and hand the human a decision that clears in one step.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/checkpoint-gates/#the-pattern)):
  - Classify every action the agent can take:
    - **Reversible**: local edits, test runs, scratch branches
    - **Irreversible**: merges, deploys, migrations, deletes
    - **Outward-facing**: external messages, published content, spend
  - Gate irreversible and outward-facing actions mechanically
  - At a gate, the agent parks the decision and continues independent work
  - Implements [Human in the Loop](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/human-in-the-loop/) for agents no one is watching
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/checkpoint-gates/#when-to-use)):
  - Pushes, merges, deploys, migrations
  - External messages and spend
  - [Unattended runs](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/unattended-runs/)
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/checkpoint-gates/#when-not-to-use)):
  - Reversible local edits already covered by [Verification Loops](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/verification-loops/)
  - Sandboxed throwaway environments
  - Gates so frequent that approval becomes a rubber stamp
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/checkpoint-gates/#anti-patterns)):
  - Approval requested by prompt text only
  - "Yes to all" fatigue
  - A card with no recommendation
  - Blocking the whole run on one decision

### [Context Handoff](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/context-handoff/)

Carry a run across compactions and sessions with a written handoff, not a transcript.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/context-handoff/#the-pattern)):
  - At a phase boundary, or before compaction, stop in a mergeable state
  - Commit the work
  - Write the handoff
  - The next session starts fresh and reads the handoff first
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/context-handoff/#when-to-use)):
  - Runs longer than one context window
  - Switching agent or model mid-run
  - A human takes over from an agent, or the reverse
  - Several agents take turns on one body of work
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/context-handoff/#when-not-to-use)):
  - Tasks that fit in one session
  - Breadcrumbs on the board already hold the full state
  - Exploratory threads where the reasoning trail matters more than the state
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/context-handoff/#anti-patterns)):
  - Automatic summary as the only memory
  - Half-implemented feature with no note
  - A handoff without evidence links
  - Pasting the transcript as the handoff
  - Letting the agent rewrite acceptance tests in the progress file

### [Correction Diagnosis](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/correction-diagnosis/)

Trace each correction to the input that caused it, and fix that input instead of the output.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/correction-diagnosis/#the-pattern)):
  - There is no universal fix for correction-heavy output: the right approach depends on the task, model, codebase, available context, and how much ambiguity the agent must resolve alone, and the cause chain below is how to find which one applies.
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/correction-diagnosis/#when-to-use)):
  - You correct the same kind of output more than once
  - Correcting output takes longer than writing it would have
  - A session needs two corrections on one point
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/correction-diagnosis/#when-not-to-use)):
  - Exploration, where variance is the point ([Reproducibility](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/reproducibility/))
  - Throwaway output you will not reuse
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/correction-diagnosis/#anti-patterns)):
  - Steering by chat correction instead of fixing the brief
  - Blaming the model before checking the inputs
  - Adding more context to fix a context problem
  - Never resetting a drifting session
  - Verifying first and framing never: a check catches the miss, but the wrong problem still gets solved

### [Delegation Fit](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/delegation-fit/)

Decide per task whether to delegate, pair, or write by hand, and brief delegated work in one message.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/delegation-fit/#the-pattern)):
  - Before prompting, decide per task: delegate, pair, or write by hand
  - Keep decisions that belong to a human with the human; decide first, then delegate the rest
  - Brief delegated work in one message with explicit non-goals
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/delegation-fit/#when-to-use)):
  - Everyday interactive work, before the first prompt
  - A feature with parts of different difficulty
  - Output from past tasks of this kind needed heavy correction
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/delegation-fit/#when-not-to-use)):
  - Multi-hour or unattended runs; use [Spec, Then Build](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/spec-then-build/)
  - Pure exploration, where the model's interpretation is the point
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/delegation-fit/#anti-patterns)):
  - Delegating the architecture decision, then correcting the architecture in review
  - Delegating work you could type faster than you could brief
  - A brief with no non-goals, so the diff grows past the task
  - Fit decided once and never revisited as models change

### [Discovery Propagation](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/discovery-propagation/)

When agents find better paths, propose improvements back to the system through review.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/discovery-propagation/#the-pattern)):
  - An agent finds a better approach, a missing capability, or a reusable lesson
  - It proposes the improvement for future use
  - A reviewer approves, edits, or rejects the proposal
  - Only approved changes are encoded and reach other sessions
  - Propagation always passes review; nothing spreads on its own
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/discovery-propagation/#when-to-use)):
  - The same friction shows up more than once
  - A lesson applies beyond the current task
  - A convention can be written down or enforced
  - There is a place to receive and review proposals
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/discovery-propagation/#when-not-to-use)):
  - **One-off quirks**: a flaky mirror today is not a rule
  - **Unverified single observations**: wait until the lesson shows up twice
  - **Facts that drift**: versions, line numbers, current owners; re-derive them instead ([Memory](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/stack/memory/))
  - **Active re-evaluation**: an area under review should not churn from new proposals mid-review
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/discovery-propagation/#anti-patterns)):
  - Insights that die with the session
  - Silent mutations without review
  - Over-propagation: noise drowns signal
  - No mechanism to receive proposals
  - Proposals with no evidence attached

### [Dogfooding](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/dogfooding/)

Validate by using your own output.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/dogfooding/#the-pattern)):
  - Before shipping a skill, prompt, workflow, or tool to others, use it yourself on real work. Discover friction firsthand.
- Use when ([#when-to-apply](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/dogfooding/#when-to-apply)):
  - New skills or prompts before sharing with the team
  - Workflows before documenting them as standards
  - Tools before recommending to clients
  - Patterns before encoding in governance
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/dogfooding/#when-not-to-use)):
  - One-off scripts no one else will run
  - You are not a realistic user; find one who is and watch them use it
  - Changes a deterministic test fully covers
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/dogfooding/#anti-patterns)):
  - Testing on synthetic examples only
  - Shipping before personal validation
  - Dogfooding once, then never again (things drift)
  - Exempting yourself from your own standards

### [Few-Shot Examples](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/few-shot-examples/)

Guide output format and style with concrete examples.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/few-shot-examples/#the-pattern)):
  - Include 2-5 examples of the input/output format you want before asking for the actual task. The model learns the pattern from examples.
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/few-shot-examples/#when-to-use)):
  - Specific output formats (JSON, markdown structures)
  - Consistent style or tone
  - Domain-specific conventions
  - When verbal descriptions of format are ambiguous
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/few-shot-examples/#when-not-to-use)):
  - The format is fully specified by a schema; use [Structured Output](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/structured-output/)
  - Reasoning models on tasks they handle zero-shot; try without examples first ([OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning-best-practices))
  - You have only one example and it is an edge case
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/few-shot-examples/#anti-patterns)):
  - Too many examples (diminishing returns, context waste)
  - Examples that contradict each other
  - Examples that are too similar (model over-fits to specifics)

### [Iterative Refinement](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/iterative-refinement/)

Improving output through successive passes.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/iterative-refinement/#the-pattern)):
  - Generate initial output, then run additional passes that:
  - Identify specific weaknesses
  - Make targeted improvements
  - Know when to stop (diminishing returns)
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/iterative-refinement/#when-to-use)):
  - Creative or complex output that benefits from revision
  - Tasks where "good enough" isn't good enough
  - When feedback loops are cheap relative to the value of improvement
  - Output that will be seen by humans and quality matters
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/iterative-refinement/#when-not-to-use)):
  - A runnable check exists; use [Verification Loops](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/verification-loops/) instead
  - The first draft already meets the bar
  - No stopping criterion can be stated
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/iterative-refinement/#anti-patterns)):
  - Infinite loops (no stopping criteria)
  - Passes that undo each other's work
  - Refining when the first draft was already good enough
  - Over-polishing low-stakes output

### [Mechanical Scaffolding](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/mechanical-scaffolding/)

Build repeatable structure once, fill with context each time.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/mechanical-scaffolding/#the-pattern)):
  - Separate what is REPEATABLE (structure, format, fields, validation) from what is VARIABLE (context, content, specifics). Build the scaffold in code. Let the LLM fill it.
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/mechanical-scaffolding/#when-to-use)):
  - You explain the same format repeatedly
  - Output shape is predictable across uses
  - Validation rules exist and can be encoded
  - You copy-paste between prompts
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/mechanical-scaffolding/#when-not-to-use)):
  - One-off tasks (no repetition to amortize)
  - Exploratory work where format is unknown
  - Tasks where the LLM should invent the structure
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/mechanical-scaffolding/#anti-patterns)):
  - **Scaffold drifts from the target schema**: the destination adds or renames a field and the scaffold keeps emitting the old shape; test the scaffold against the real schema
  - **Validation duplicated in prompt and code**: the two copies disagree over time; keep rules in code and send only failures back to the model
  - **Over-scaffolding exploratory work**: locking a format before it is understood forces bad structure; scaffold after the shape repeats

### [Multi-Model Consensus](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/multi-model-consensus/)

Running the same task across multiple models and comparing results.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/multi-model-consensus/#the-pattern)):
  - Run the same task through multiple models (or the same model with different prompts/temperatures), then:
  - Compare outputs for agreement
  - Flag divergence for human review or deeper investigation
  - Use consensus as a confidence signal
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/multi-model-consensus/#when-to-use)):
  - Factual questions where correctness matters
  - Classification or categorization tasks
  - Any task where "the model might be wrong" is a real concern
  - Calibrating confidence before acting on output
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/multi-model-consensus/#when-not-to-use)):
  - A deterministic check exists; run it instead
  - Open-ended writing, where outputs differ by design
  - All candidate models share the same blind spot (same training data, same missing context)
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/multi-model-consensus/#anti-patterns)):
  - Using consensus to avoid thinking ("they all agreed, must be right")
  - Ignoring the dissenting model when two agree and one doesn't
  - Running consensus on tasks where models share the same blind spots

### [Pipeline Orchestration](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/pipeline-orchestration/)

Chain stages with explicit contracts and a gate at every handoff.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/pipeline-orchestration/#the-pattern)):
  - Structure work as sequential stages
  - Each stage has an input contract, an output contract, and a gate
  - Output of stage N becomes input to stage N+1 only after its gate passes
  - Anthropic calls this prompt chaining: each call processes the previous output, with programmatic checks on intermediate steps ([Building Effective Agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents))
  - It trades latency for accuracy by making each call an easier task (same source)
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/pipeline-orchestration/#when-to-use)):
  - The task splits cleanly into fixed, known phases
  - Intermediate outputs are worth keeping as checkpoints
  - Stages need different skills, tools, or model tiers
  - A failure should be traceable to one stage
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/pipeline-orchestration/#when-not-to-use)):
  - **Exploratory work**: phases are unknown until you start; use an agent loop or [Subagent Fanout](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/subagent-fanout/) for breadth
  - **Single-step tasks**: a pipeline adds handoffs with nothing to hand off
  - **Constant back-and-forth**: stages that must renegotiate each other's output belong in one stage
  - **Parallel, independent work**: fan out instead of queueing
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/pipeline-orchestration/#anti-patterns)):
  - **No gates**: a bad spec flows into a bad implementation that passes its own weak checks; errors compound downstream
  - **No resumability**: a stage-4 failure restarts from stage 1 and repays every token
  - **Coupled stages**: one stage cannot run without the internals of another
  - **Monolithic stages**: a "do everything" stage hides which part failed
  - **Gates that always pass**: a check nobody has seen fail proves nothing

### [Progress Breadcrumbs](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/progress-breadcrumbs/)

Record an agent's progress on a shared work board, not in the chat.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/progress-breadcrumbs/#the-pattern)):
  - One board item per plan step
  - The card moves as the work moves: To Do, In Progress, Blocked, Done
  - The agent adds a short comment per step: what is done, the evidence, what is next
  - The board, not the transcript, is the record of the run
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/progress-breadcrumbs/#when-to-use)):
  - Runs longer than one session
  - Several agents or humans need status on the same work
  - Work must survive a crash, a restart, or context compaction
  - Checkpoints are asynchronous: the human answers hours later
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/progress-breadcrumbs/#when-not-to-use)):
  - Short tasks that finish in one session
  - Private scratch exploration nobody else needs to follow
  - Boards nobody reads
  - Trackers where each comment pages people (high notification cost)
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/progress-breadcrumbs/#anti-patterns)):
  - Status that lives only in chat scrollback
  - One giant comment at the end instead of one per step
  - Breadcrumbs without evidence: "done" with no command, run, or commit
  - Log spam: every tool call posted as a comment
  - Secrets, credentials, or personal data in comments

### [Prompt Regression Testing](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/prompt-regression/)

Detect when prompt changes break existing behavior.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/prompt-regression/#the-pattern)):
  - Maintain a suite of inputs with expected outcomes. Run it against every prompt or model change before deploying. Compare to a recorded baseline.
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/prompt-regression/#when-to-use)):
  - Prompts that have been tuned over time
  - Production prompts with known good behavior
  - Before updating models or prompt templates ([Deliberate Currency](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/deliberate-currency/))
  - When multiple people edit the same prompts
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/prompt-regression/#when-not-to-use)):
  - Throwaway prompts that will not run again
  - Exploration and brainstorming paths marked exempt from reproducibility ([Reproducibility](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/reproducibility/))
  - Before the expected behavior is settled: tests would lock in a guess
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/prompt-regression/#anti-patterns)):
  - Testing only the happy path
  - Exact string matching on free prose
  - Single runs on nondeterministic output
  - No baseline (cannot tell if a change helped or hurt)
  - Running tests only manually

### [RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/rag/)

Ground responses in retrieved context.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/rag/#the-pattern)):
  - Before generating, retrieve relevant documents/data and include them in context. The model generates based on provided sources rather than training data alone.
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/rag/#when-to-use)):
  - Questions about your specific data (docs, code, logs)
  - Current information (training data is stale)
  - Verifiable claims (source can be cited)
  - Domain-specific knowledge not in training
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/rag/#when-not-to-use)):
  - The answer is in the model's general knowledge and does not change
  - The whole source fits in context; include it directly
  - Retrieval quality is untested; fix retrieval first
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/rag/#anti-patterns)):
  - Retrieving too much (floods context, buries signal)
  - Retrieving irrelevant content (model tries to use it anyway)
  - Not testing retrieval (generation fails silently on bad retrieval)
  - Assuming RAG fixes hallucination (it reduces, doesn't eliminate)

### [Reviewable Output](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/reviewable-output/)

Shape delegated code and documents so a human can review them against intent, not from scratch.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/reviewable-output/#the-pattern)):
  - Ask for output in a shape that is cheap to review
  - Machines check syntax, style, and tests first; the human reviews intent and design
  - Large work arrives in stages, each a smaller review than the whole
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/reviewable-output/#when-to-use)):
  - Delegation fits, but review of the result is the slow step
  - Diffs that touch several concerns at once
  - Changes a reviewer must read against a repo convention
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/reviewable-output/#when-not-to-use)):
  - One-line or throwaway changes
  - Exploration spikes that will be discarded
  - Output a deterministic check fully covers, with no design decision in it
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/reviewable-output/#anti-patterns)):
  - One diff that mixes a refactor with a behavior change
  - "Tests pass" with no command or output
  - Human review spent on formatting that a linter owns
  - Reviewing the implementation before anyone approved the plan

### [Self-Critique](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/self-critique/)

Have the model evaluate its own output against criteria.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/self-critique/#the-pattern)):
  - After generating output, prompt the same or a follow-up call to critique the output against specific criteria, then revise based on the findings.
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/self-critique/#when-to-use)):
  - Quality-sensitive outputs with criteria you can write down
  - Style, completeness, and format checks
  - When external feedback is available to ground the critique (test results, linter output, a validator)
  - As a lighter alternative to Adversarial Review on low-stakes work
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/self-critique/#when-not-to-use)):
  - Reasoning correctness with no external signal (math, logic, factual claims): the model tends to confirm or break its own answer
  - High-stakes output: use [Adversarial Review](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/adversarial-review/) or deterministic checks
  - Simple tasks where a critique pass adds tokens without adding value
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/self-critique/#anti-patterns)):
  - "Is this good?" as the critique prompt: the critique praises the output or lists generic tweaks
  - Self-critique of reasoning with no external signal: the revision flips a correct answer
  - Revisions not tied to a failed item: the rewrite changes things no finding named
  - Self-critique as the only gate on high-stakes output: the model's blind spots about its own errors ship unchecked

### [Spec, Then Build](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/spec-then-build/)

Agree a written spec and reviewed plan before an agent executes.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/spec-then-build/#the-pattern)):
  - Three phases: **spec**, then **plan review**, then **execute**
  - The spec is a written agreement, not a long phase
  - Execution starts only after the plan survives review
  - Applies [Problem Before Prescription](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/problem-before-prescription/) to agent work
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/spec-then-build/#when-to-use)):
  - Multi-hour or [unattended runs](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/unattended-runs/)
  - Uncertain solution space
  - Work that spans several context windows ([Context Handoff](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/context-handoff/))
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/spec-then-build/#when-not-to-use)):
  - One-line or throwaway changes
  - Solution fully known and the human holds decisive context: prescribe, and say why
  - Pure exploration: step 1 is the exploration
  - The ticket already states problem, constraints, checkable criteria, and scope
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/spec-then-build/#anti-patterns)):
  - "Make it work" as the only criterion
  - Spec prescribes the implementation instead of the problem
  - Skipping plan review, then steering by correction in chat
  - Plan written once, or kept only in chat

### [Step-Level Routing](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/step-level-routing/)

Route each step inside an agent trajectory to a model tier and reasoning effort.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/step-level-routing/#the-pattern)):
  - Choose model tier and reasoning effort per request inside an agent trajectory
  - Do not fix one model per agent or per task
  - Two dials per step: **model tier** and **reasoning effort**
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/step-level-routing/#when-to-use)):
  - Long trajectories mixing cheap steps (search, read) with hard ones (plan, review)
  - The harness or gateway can switch models mid-trajectory
  - You measure cost per outcome, so you can tell whether routing helps
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/step-level-routing/#when-not-to-use)):
  - Short tasks where a switch costs more than it saves
  - Workloads that depend on a long, warm prompt cache
  - No outcome measurement to catch misroutes
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/step-level-routing/#anti-patterns)):
  - Optimizing per-call price while total cost per outcome rises
  - Switching models every step and paying for cold caches
  - Flipping top-level effort every step; Anthropic advises holding it constant within a cached conversation ([Anthropic effort docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort))
  - Where the model supports it, change effort per message instead; that keeps the prompt cache
  - Routing on input length instead of step type

### [Structured Output](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/structured-output/)

Force output into a defined schema.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/structured-output/#the-pattern)):
  - Constrain model output to a defined format (JSON, XML, typed schema) that code can parse and validate.
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/structured-output/#when-to-use)):
  - Output feeds into downstream code
  - You need specific fields, not free-form text
  - Validation and error handling matter
  - Pipeline stages depend on a consistent format
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/structured-output/#when-not-to-use)):
  - Human-facing prose: a schema adds friction and flattens the writing
  - Exploratory brainstorming: the shape of a good answer is not known yet
  - One-off questions where a person reads the answer directly
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/structured-output/#anti-patterns)):
  - Over-complicated schemas that are hard to fill correctly and hard to debug
  - No validation on parse (trusting without checking)
  - Treating a schema-valid response as a correct response
  - Forcing structure where prose would be clearer

### [Subagent Fanout](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/subagent-fanout/)

Split independent work across subagents that read widely and return compact results.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/subagent-fanout/#the-pattern)):
  - A coordinator splits a task into independent slices
  - Each subagent gets one slice, its own context window, and a return contract
  - Subagents return summaries or structured results, not their raw reading
  - The coordinator checks coverage, merges, and decides what happens next
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/subagent-fanout/#when-to-use)):
  - Parallel, independent strands: review each file, audit each service, research each question
  - Reading that would flood the main context
  - Post-implementation verification in a fresh context ([Adversarial Review](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/adversarial-review/))
  - Wall-clock time matters and slices do not wait on each other
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/subagent-fanout/#when-not-to-use)):
  - **Dependent subtasks**: B needs A's output; use [Pipeline Orchestration](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/pipeline-orchestration/)
  - **Tightly coupled coding**: Anthropic notes most coding tasks have fewer truly parallel parts than research ([source](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system))
  - **Shared implicit decisions**: subagents that cannot see each other make conflicting assumptions, and the merge inherits the conflict ([Cognition, Don't Build Multi-Agents](https://cognition.com/blog/dont-build-multi-agents))
  - **Briefing costs more than doing**: a two-file change is faster inline
  - **Shared mutable state**: agents editing the same branch or files
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/subagent-fanout/#anti-patterns)):
  - **Trusting summaries over artifacts**: a subagent says "tests pass"; check the exit code or the file
  - **Agents sharing a branch**: parallel edits collide; give each writer its own worktree or keep writers to one
  - **Coordinator re-reads everything**: this cancels the context win; spot-check cited evidence instead
  - **No partial-failure plan**: one failed slice should re-run alone, not restart the fanout
  - **Fanout by habit**: spawning agents for work one thread would finish sooner

### [Task Routing](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/task-routing/)

Match each task to the smallest model tier that reliably succeeds.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/task-routing/#the-pattern)):
  - Route each task to a model tier by complexity, cost, and capability needs
  - Default to the smallest tier that reliably succeeds on your evals
  - Escalate when the router is uncertain or a check fails
  - Route to tier names in code; map tiers to models in one config
  - Fit capability, not only size: judge each task type on its own evals ([Model Selection](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/stack/models/#selection-criteria))
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/task-routing/#when-to-use)):
  - Workloads with mixed complexity
  - Cost or latency is a constraint on some paths
  - You have access to more than one model
  - You can measure outcomes per task type ([Evaluation](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/stack/evaluation/))
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/task-routing/#when-not-to-use)):
  - **Single-model access**: nothing to route between
  - **Uniform workload**: every task needs the same tier, so a router adds only failure modes
  - **No outcome measurement**: you cannot see misroutes, so savings are guesses
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/task-routing/#anti-patterns)):
  - Biggest model for everything (cost explosion)
  - Cheapest model for everything (quality collapse)
  - Routing on input length instead of task complexity
  - Product IDs scattered through code, so model changes need a code search
  - No fallback when the preferred model is unavailable

### [Unattended Runs](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/unattended-runs/)

Launch an agent to work for hours without a human watching each step.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/unattended-runs/#the-pattern)):
  - Design up front, then a long stretch with no one watching
  - Human attention moves to written checkpoints and the end of the run
  - The run ends on a stop condition decided before launch, not on someone noticing
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/unattended-runs/#when-to-use)):
  - Checkable acceptance criteria exist
  - Verification is automated ([Verification Loops](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/verification-loops/))
  - Irreversible actions are gated
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/unattended-runs/#when-not-to-use)):
  - Exploratory work with no checkable win
  - No automated verification: the human becomes the loop
  - Irreversible actions with no gate
  - Task shorter than the setup
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/unattended-runs/#anti-patterns)):
  - No stop condition
  - Uncapped retries
  - Checking in every ten minutes
  - Treating the timebox as a delivery deadline: the run stops at the cap, finished or not

### [Verification Loops](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/verification-loops/)

Generate, run a check, and repair until it passes or a stop condition fires.

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/verification-loops/#the-pattern)):
  - Generate output, then run a check
  - On failure, feed the specific failure back and try again
  - Stop when the check passes or a stop condition fires
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/verification-loops/#when-to-use)):
  - Output has machine-checkable criteria
  - First-attempt accuracy is not reliable enough
  - A check costs less than the error it catches
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/verification-loops/#when-not-to-use)):
  - No machine-checkable criteria exist
  - The check costs more than the error
  - The failure is a spec problem; fix the spec, not the output
  - Subjective quality without a rubric; use [Adversarial Review](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/adversarial-review/)
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/verification-loops/#anti-patterns)):
  - The loop edits the test until it passes
  - Error output truncated, so the model repairs the wrong thing
  - The prompt grows every iteration; send the latest failure, not the history
